correctness.rationale: Character orthogonality reduces the sixth moment to exact triple-fiber collision counts. In characteristic 3, s≠0 fibers have q elements, while s=0 fibers have q/2q according to negative-square condition, giving M(1)=q⁴+q³−q². Pair-correlation kernels K(t,t)=2q²−q and K(t,u)=q² for t≠u, and weighted pair L(t,t)=q², L(t,u)=q²+q, yield the quadratic expansion. Normalize by (q⁻¹Σ|f|²)^3, split h=u+iv to obtain the two positive transverse coefficients for every q>=3. Uniform finite-dimensional Taylor bounds justify sharp local inf and zero scalar modes. Independently enumerated all GF(9) triples and pair kernels: M(1)=7209, K_diag=153, K_off=81, L_diag=81, L_off=90, matching theory. GF(3) finite-difference half-Hessians reproduced 14/9 real and 2/3 imaginary for h=(1,−1,0).

Related paraboloid L⁴ Hessians concern different quadratic surfaces and moment exponents. No inspected source supplies the all-n characteristic-three two-band Hessian.

value.rationale: The characteristic-three case is a naturally excluded boundary of the established sharp parabola sixth-moment theory. Its collapsed triple-convolution fibers create a new arithmetic Hessian phenomenon, and the exact two-band positive spectrum gives a quantitative local stability constant for every GF(3^n), independent of the still-open global maximization problem.

limitations: Local Hessian and small-distance sharp coefficient only; no global extension norm or global extremizer classification
